newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel shrugs off India cancellation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel shrugs off India cancellation.

text.p: Gas oil (diesel) prices were firm in Singapore on Wednesday, despite India's cancellation of a buy tender, with the market finding support from the west, traders said.

Gas oil prices were assessed at $27.05 per barrel free-on-board (FOB) Singapore on Tuesday, down 70 cents from Monday, after news that state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) had cancelled its November buy tender.

Traders said they expected assessments to rebound on Wednesday as the Singapore swaps market was much stronger in the wake of a firm gas oil futures market in London and a strong physical market in the west.
"IOC's rare move to cancel its regular monthly tender led to a knee jerk reaction. Nervous players sold the market down aggressively," one trader said.

The strong selling was seen in hectic trading on the swaps market where October gas oil traded to an intraday low of $26.72 on Tuesday afternoon. But the price rebounded sharply late in the day to an intraday high of $27.40 as players bought the market back, brokers said.
October gas oil swaps traded earlier on Wednesday at $27.43 and were currently quoted at $27.40-$27.50, they said.
The firmness of the derivative market was expected to support the physical market, which does not normally trade signficantly until London opens, market sources said.
"The market is well supported by high prices in the West," one trader said.
Strong western prices have attracted spot MidEast cargoes to East and South Africa and the Mediterrenean markets, taking supplies away from Asia, traders said.
"I've not seen any spot exports from the AG (Gulf) to Singapore in September and I don't think any would be exported in October," one refiner said.
Heating oil prices in the United States were also likely to stay strong for the rest of the year due to low stocks and peak winter demand, traders said.

The latest American Petroleum Institute (API) data revealed a modest 235,000-barrel distillate build for the week ending September 13, putting stocks at 21.5 million barrels below last year at 112.058 million barrels.
The market was seeing support from China, which recently bought cargoes at above $200 per tonne cost-and-freight (c-and-f), traders said.
"China breached a psychological mark when it bought at above $200," a refiner said.
Late last week, China paid $213 per tonne c-and-f for a gas oil cargo from Japan and early this week was willing to pay up to $220, traders said.
Chinese traders have since lowered their bids as prices in Singapore fell, but they were expected to keep the fob price supported at $27.00, traders said.
